name: Damnation A.D.
label: Revelation
lede: Ken Olden spent his days in D.C. youth crew band [[Battery]] and his nights in the same house tuning down to C for Damnation A.D., a darker band that loved The Cure as much as Crowbar.

eras.title: A studio project with a tagalong singer
eras.text: Ken Olden was already a D.C. straight edge fixture, playing in Battery alongside Brian McTernan. Damnation began as Olden's studio project out of the ashes of Worlds Collide, and Brian's brother Mike, who'd never sung in a band, ended up at the microphone.

years.big: I have zero musical ability. I do what Ken tells me.
years.src: No Echo · Performer Mag · Gut Feeling
years.h: A studio project picks up a singer who has never sung
years.p: Mike McTernan, there through his brother [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]], gets the microphone while Ken Olden plays every instrument himself. That's McTernan describing his own job.
years.xp: Olden and guitarist Hillel Halloway had played together in Worlds Collide and wanted something heavier. Olden played drums for the band's live shows for nearly a year before he got off the kit and onto guitar, and he says that's when things clicked.

years.h: Another punk band owns the name, so the A.D. goes on
years.p: Damnation was taken, so Ken Olden and Mike McTernan add the initials.

eras.title: Down to C in a D.C. house
eras.text: Damnation A.D.'s debut came out on Jade Tree, whose co-founder Tim Owen went to high school with Mike McTernan. The band made it in the house they lived in, with drums in an attic bedroom, then toured with Ignite and Earth Crisis.

years.h: No More Dreams of Happy Endings · Jade Tree
years.p: Recorded over a month at Ken Olden's SNP Studio in D.C., in the house the band lived in. The opener, Two Steps Down, is named for the detuning: Damnation played in C.
years.xp:
Alex Merchlinsky's attic bedroom was the drum room, for its wood. Olden wrote most songs on drums first and ran everything through a 50-watt Marshall JCM800 and a Turbo RAT. The influences were Drive Like Jehu, Unwound, Girls Against Boys and [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]].

A 45-second Chopin Funeral March had appeared on early 7"s, including a split with Walleye; the CD has the whole piece, placed as a palate cleanser. [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]]'s Jay Yuenger told Olden Time Does Not Rest had one of the sickest riffs he'd heard.
play: No More Dreams of Happy Endings

years.p: Damnation A.D.'s second Jade Tree release, a year after No More Dreams of Happy Endings.

years.h: Stage fright on the road with [[Ignite|4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc]] and [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]]
years.p: Mike McTernan sometimes throws up before sets and says it all goes away after the first line. His best tour memories are 3 a.m. Denny's runs with the other bands.

eras.title: Revelation, Inner Ear, and an ending
eras.text: Damnation A.D. moved to Revelation for a second album, cut at Inner Ear with D.C. hardcore royalty in earshot. The band ended the same year.

years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] in earshot while Mike McTernan sang. Wait for a Day opens on a synth.
years.xp: Revelation's first pressing was just 223 copies on grey vinyl. A 2023 collector's rundown of the Revelation catalog called it apocalyptic and way ahead of its time.

years.big: I think it was just time.
years.h: Ken Olden moves on, and Damnation A.D. stops
years.p: Mike McTernan on the ending. Olden was busy with [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]], and McTernan says he'd spent years putting off dealing with his mental health.
years.xp: McTernan later joined When Tigers Fight in Springfield, Massachusetts. Working with Olden on that project is what brought the two back together.

eras.title: Olden goes youth crew again
eras.text: Ken Olden joined the youth crew revival band Better Than a Thousand with the same amp, guitars and settings as Damnation A.D., just a different tuning. Revelation kept the last album in print.

years.h: Revelation calls the orange pressing its last
years.p: 331 copies of Kingdom of Lost Souls on orange vinyl, billed as final. It wasn't.

eras.title: Back, with Fall Out Boy on the record
eras.text: Damnation A.D. reunited on Victory Records and packed the comeback with guests, two of them from Fall Out Boy.

years.h: Fall Out Boy drop in on In This Life or the Next
years.p: [[Pete Wentz|26cea341-dfab-483f-9cdb-8de82da81019]] and [[Patrick Stump|563abe5e-06b1-430d-99d4-7abf981c6e5a]] of Fall Out Boy guest on If You Could Remember, Wes Eisold on Don't Feel a Thing, and Earth Crisis's Karl Buechner and Darkest Hour's John Henry appear too.
years.xp: McTernan said the guests were people who had influenced him to start playing music again. The video for Knot came out the same year.
play: In This Life or the Next

years.cap: Damnation A.D. at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, January 6, 2008
years.h: Nine years on, Olden and McTernan play shows again
years.p: Back as a live band behind the Victory record, with Ken Olden and Mike McTernan out front.

eras.title: Pornography, finally
eras.text: Revelation pressed Kingdom of Lost Souls in bigger numbers than ever, and Olden and McTernan finished the project they'd talked about since the start: all of The Cure's Pornography, tuned down even further.

years.h: Revelation presses 1,012 white copies of Kingdom of Lost Souls
years.p: More than four times the 223 copies of the first pressing in 1998.
Damnation A.D. cover all of The Cure's album on a Record Store Day LP: 800 copies on clear blue vinyl, worked on in secret. Olden drops the top string to A# for it.
years.xp: The Cure's 1982 album was one of the band's founding influences. It was Damnation A.D.'s first new release in a decade. Olden says there are still finished Damnation songs sitting around without vocals or lyrics.
